summary.intent: Push forward the Callisto v1 implementation stack without pausing, get all outstanding work (schema handling, lockfile refresh, history/pnpm fixes, setup-action installer, recovery semantics, native auth) validated through full CI and independent review, then safely reconcile local main with origin/main so a PR stack could be opened.
summary.outcome: Full CI (1,851 tests, ~93.4% coverage) passed after multiple review-driven fixes (lockfile ecosystem detection, HEAD-lookup guard, unique diagnostic codes, npm/PyPI/Bun credential isolation, prerelease retry-guard edge cases); local main was rebased and realigned to exactly match origin/main while all v1 work was moved onto work/v1-implementation-stack; only the 6-file T11 setup-installer slice was staged and committed after explicit user confirmation — no push or remote PR was made.

repo: Repo has a `test_all_diagnostic_codes_are_unique` guard that fails the build if a new diagnostic code collides with an existing one (caught E250/others colliding before landing on E304).
A companion repository guard requires every diagnostic code to have user-facing documentation in the docs catalog, checked separately from the uniqueness test.
`just ci` is the full gate: formatting, clippy, full nextest suite, workflow-policy mutation checks, and a 90% coverage threshold (observed ~93.4-93.5%).

Graph crate has registry-observation tests that shell out to real `cargo info`; when run concurrently/sandboxed they fail with CommandFailed due to sharing one hermetic Cargo registry fixture — they pass when run serially or with normal cache access, and are not real regressions.
Native workspace integration tests (uv/pnpm) can hit sandbox permission errors opening existing package manager caches; redirecting the cache to a writable temp dir resolves it without code changes.

T05 prerelease `exit` finalization needed a state distinction: the interrupted-run guard (E121) must treat 'still has prerelease versions to finalize' differently from 'already wrote stable versions and should refuse retry', otherwise it false-positives on normal `pre exit` reruns.

Callisto delegates publishing to native package managers (npm/pnpm/Yarn/Bun); those may run package.json lifecycle hooks (prepare/prepublishOnly/postpublish) which inherit publish credentials like NPM_TOKEN — this is intentional and should not be suppressed or gated by Callisto.

code.finding: Installer previously could bypass a pinned version by mistaking a nearby dependency checkout for the actual Callisto source; fix validates the local source is a genuine Callisto checkout before honoring pinned versions.

T04-LOCK: lockfile refresh/staging must be derived from every actual write target (bump manifests, dependency rewrite targets, platform writes, optional-dependency writes, inherited Cargo targets), not just the primary manifest.

workflow: When told 'do not pause', still stop for explicit user decisions that change security/behavioral trade-offs (e.g., asked before deciding whether to alter npm publish lifecycle-hook credential exposure) rather than unilaterally changing release semantics.

Adversarial/independent re-review after a green full CI run repeatedly surfaced real edge cases (HEAD-lookup guard, prerelease pre.json staging order, npm credential file exposure, staged-vs-disk version detection) — full test pass does not imply review-complete; budget for at least one review pass before calling work PR-ready.

When reconciling a diverged local main with origin/main without losing uncommitted work: stash with -u, create a backup branch, rebase only the unique committed delta onto the fetched origin/main, resolve conflicts, restore the stash, then move all remaining uncommitted work to a dedicated feature branch before fast-forwarding local main to origin/main.
Sandbox environment intermittently blocks writes to `.git/index` (staging/commit operations), requiring an elevated permission retry rather than indicating a real error.

friction: Sandbox blocked `.git/index` writes multiple times (staging the T11 slice, creating a safety backup branch, committing after user confirmation), each requiring a retry with elevated workspace Git access.

False-positive test failures from environment issues (concurrent cargo registry fixture sharing, uv cache sandbox permissions, restricted network access to crates.io) repeatedly interrupted CI runs and required diagnosis before concluding they weren't real regressions.
Diagnostic code collisions (E250 and other attempted codes) required multiple iterations before landing on a free code (E304), plus a follow-up fix for missing documentation.
Implementation tracker/ledger was stale and understated completed work, requiring manual reconciliation against actual code state.

Local main had diverged from origin/main by 4 commits (0.9.0/0.10.0 releases, #169/#170) while carrying 84 uncommitted paths, entangling unrelated local-only files (.claude, .entire, .gemini settings) with real implementation work.
open_items: Stack is not yet split into reviewable PR-sized commits beyond the single committed T11 installer slice; ~70 files across multiple topics still need to be divided into PRs with matching changesets/specs/task records.
Owner decisions in plan D01 still needed before finalizing contracts for canonical identity, release ownership/retries, Python artifact recovery, and workflow generation.

Remaining v1 scope beyond the current batch: interrupted-version recovery follow-ups, canonical identity, release-effect retries/completion barriers, Python artifact recovery and registry routing, generated workflow/build boundaries, production-matrix/onboarding evidence.

Operator docs/spec were updated to state the lifecycle-hook trust boundary (package owners control prepublish/postpublish hooks); ensure this documentation lands in the eventual PR alongside the auth changes.
No push or remote PR has been opened yet; T11 is the only committed slice pending further stack assembly and user go-ahead to push.
